title: Words that outgrow their container wrap instead of hanging out of it
goal: When a label is wider than the box it lives in, the words wrap onto a second line and the box grows downward, instead of running out past the edge where nobody can read them. Today a button with a ceiling on its width shows its label hanging off the side.
notes: Follow-up from queue/audits/2026-09-05-group-size-limits.json. Limits landed 2026-09-05 (GroupLayout.minWidth/maxWidth/minHeight/maxHeight, GroupFlow.holding). The ceiling case deliberately leaves the words starting at the near edge and overhanging the far one, because clipping loses them and centring pushes them off the near edge too. Text measurement and re-wrap already exist for a stretched label in a stack (see the reflowPasses comment in GroupLayoutEditing); the missing piece is handing a capped width to a label that is NOT set to stretch.
acceptance: A text layer inside a group whose width is capped wraps at that width rather than overhanging it
The group grows taller as the words wrap, unless its height is capped too
A label that fits changes in no way at all
Tests cover wrapping at a ceiling, at a typed width, and the no-change case in PhotonzCore before the app code is written

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The mock does not cover this; it comes from the size-limits audit complaint, so there is nothing to copy. (2) The expected answer is the one every stylesheet already gives: a max width makes the words wrap and the box grow downward. Building anything else would surprise a first-time user. (3) The trap is the one-way door: if the flow narrows the label and forgets it did, clearing the ceiling leaves the label stuck on two lines in a tall narrow pill, which reads as broken. That is exactly the step the last audit asked for (empty the box and press Return), so it would be hit immediately. Fix: the flow records that IT narrowed the label, undoes that at the top of every pass, and re-derives. (4) Second trap: the ceiling test is run against the label as it currently is, so a wrapped label measures as if it fitted, the limit stops biting and the next pass un-wraps it, forever. Fix comes free from (3): undo first, then measure. (5) Cut from scope: a row stack holding TWO labels that both outgrow it has no single answer (each would be sized against the other), so a row wraps at most one label and the rest is left as it is. (6) Not touched: a paragraph somebody deliberately dragged narrower. Its width is a choice, not a derivation.

Built in PhotonzCore, tests first. GroupFlow.placed now runs in three steps: undo anything a container narrowed last time, settle the WIDTH (holding is split per axis so the width is decided before the words break), wrap the labels that outgrow the room, then settle the HEIGHT from what the wrap actually came out at. Room per label: the whole width across for a free group and a column stack, one cell for a grid, and what the other pieces leave for a row stack (one label only). Layer.wrappedByItsContainer records that the flow, not a person, chose that width; resized() drops it the moment somebody drags or types a width of their own. 13 new tests in GroupTextWrapTests, 3637 green.

Adversarial review of the BUILT thing, on the probe app (Screen Recording granted, real captures). Found a real regression and fixed it: with a ceiling of 56 on the starter Button, CoreText broke the single word Button into But over ton and the second line was cut off by the pill. Wrapping cannot help a word that has nothing to break at, so textWrapped now never narrows a label below TextMeasurement.widestWord: a word too long for the room hangs out of it exactly as it did before, which is the honest answer and the one every stylesheet gives. Re-ran size-limits-walk to confirm the Button case is what it was. Also cut the cost: the wrap asks the expensive question (is this width the container's to decide) only about labels that actually do not fit, so a screen full of labels that fit pays nothing.

Verified: wrap-at-a-ceiling-walk renders for step 1 (no ceiling) and step 3 (ceiling cleared) are byte identical, so clearing the ceiling really does give the words their line back rather than leaving them stuck on two. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-05-words-that-wrap.json with two real window captures.

A label in a group with a capped or typed width now wraps inside that width and the group grows downward, instead of running out past the far edge. Never past its widest single word, so a word that cannot break hangs out as before rather than coming apart in the middle. The flow records that it chose the width, so clearing the ceiling gives the words their one line back. PhotonzCore only (GroupFlow, TextMeasurement, Layer.wrappedByItsContainer); 13 new tests, 3637 green; verified on the probe app with real window captures and a byte-identical before/after render.
